data.name: Afeen
data.gender_notes: Afeen is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'afn' meaning 'soft, tender, gentle', Afeen is a beautiful and soothing name for a baby boy. The name Afeen carries the meaning “Soft, Tender” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Afeen usually hope their child will grow to embody soft, tender and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Afeen is a name that symbolizes tenderness, compassion, and kindness. It is believed to bring peace and tranquility to those who bear the name.
data.etymology: Afeen belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soft, Tender.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Afeen total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Afeen holds a profound cultural significance, as tenderness, compassion, and kindness are highly valued traits in Islamic and Arabic cultures. The name evokes images of gentleness and nurturing, making it an ideal choice for parents who aspire to raise a compassionate and caring child. In various Islamic communities around the world, the name Afeen is celebrated as a symbol of love and tenderness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Afeen holds deep significance, as it reflects the gentle and compassionate nature of God. In many Islamic traditions, God is referred to as Ar-Rahman (The Most Merciful) and Ar-Rahim (The Compassionate). By giving their child the name Afeen, parents may be hoping to imbue their child with these same divine qualities – to be a gentle, tender, and compassionate soul. The name Afeen also has a connection to the concept of ruh (spirit) in Islamic belief. Just as the name evokes tenderness in human relations, it can also be seen as a reminder of the tender and loving nature of the divine spirit that resides within every human being.
